name: Misner Space
description: Minkowski space identified under a boost, flat everywhere. A contracting universe whose closed direction turns from space into time across a horizon of closed null geodesics, with closed timelike curves through every event beyond it.
history: Misner space is Minkowski space with each event identified with its images under repeated boosts along one direction, $x$, so that it is flat everywhere and its closed timelike curves come from the identification alone [misner1967, li1998]. Charles Misner introduced it in 1967 in a lecture on Taub-NUT space as "a counterexample to almost anything" [misner1967]. It is the flat model of Taub-NUT, the vacuum spacetime Misner had joined in 1963 from Abraham Taub's universe and the space of Ezra Newman, Louis Tamburino, and Theodore Unti, whose horizon has finite curvature and incomplete geodesics and beyond which closed timelike curves pass through every event [misner1963, hawking1973, hiscock1982].¶In Misner's coordinates $T$ and $\psi$, periodic in $\psi$ with period $\psi_0$, the boost has rapidity $\psi_0/2$, and the coordinates cover half the plane of $t$ and $x$: the past light cone of the origin, where $T < 0$, and the wedge $x > c|t|$ beside it, where $T > 0$ [levanony2011]. Where $T < 0$ the circles of constant $T$, $y$, and $z$ are spacelike, and space is a flat universe whose closed direction, of circumference $\psi_0\sqrt{-T}$, shrinks as $T$ climbs toward zero [levanony2011]. At $T = 0$ the same circles are closed null geodesics, which form the chronology horizon, and where $T > 0$ they are closed timelike curves, one through every event [levanony2011, li1998].¶Misner gave two ways to extend the region $T < 0$ across its horizon, into the wedge $x > c|t|$ or into its mirror image $x < -c|t|$ [misner1967, levanony2011]. Stephen Hawking and George Ellis showed in 1973 that the two extensions are inequivalent, each flat and Hausdorff, and that extending across both horizons at once gives a flat spacetime that is not Hausdorff [hawking1973]. The observers at rest in the covering Minkowski space split into two families at the horizon: those at $x > 0$ cross it at a finite $\psi$ into the region of closed timelike curves, while those at $x < 0$ wind round the closed direction without end and reach $T = 0$ only as $\psi \to \infty$, after a finite proper time [levanony2011]. In the other extension the two families exchange these roles [levanony2011].¶The stress energy of a quantum field diverges on the chronology horizon in the states William Hiscock and Deborah Konkowski studied on Misner space in 1982, in those Sung-Won Kim and Kip Thorne studied on a wormhole time machine in 1991, and, as Claes Cramer and Bernard Kay proved in 1996, in every state of Sergey Sushkov's field twisted by a phase round the closed direction [hiscock1982, kim1991, sushkov1997, cramer1996]. Hawking conjectured in 1992 that the expectation value of the stress energy tensor grows large as timelike curves become almost closed, that its back reaction prevents them from forming, and that the laws of physics do not allow closed timelike curves to appear [hawking1992]. Li-Xin Li and J. Richard Gott found in 1998 that when the boost has rapidity $2\pi$, that is $\psi_0 = 4\pi$, the Rindler vacuum of the covering space summed over its images has a renormalized stress energy that vanishes at every event off the horizon, and a particle detector moving along a geodesic in it registers nothing [li1998].¶James Grant showed in 1993 that, away from the strings, Gott's time machine of two cosmic strings [gott1991] is a generalised Misner space, identified under a boost combined with a shift across it [grant1993, li1998]. On it the vacuum stress energy of a conformally coupled scalar field diverges weakly at the chronology horizon and more strongly on the polarised hypersurfaces inside it, strongly enough, Grant argued, to alter the spacetime before quantum gravity comes into play [grant1993]. Thorne titled his contribution to the symposium held at the University of Maryland in May 1993 for the sixtieth birthdays of Misner and Dieter Brill "Misner space as a prototype for almost any pathology" [thorne1993misner].¶A rigid object carried into the region of closed timelike curves of two dimensional Misner space inevitably collides with itself, as Dana Levanony and Amos Ori found in 2011 [levanony2011]. In four dimensions an object moving across the direction of the boost has a wide range of orbits free of any self collision [levanony2011]. In string theory Misner space is the Lorentzian orbifold of the plane by a boost, which Micha Berkooz, Boris Pioline, and Moshe Rozali call "one of the simplest examples of a cosmological singularity in string theory" [berkooz2004]. They found in 2004 two kinds of winding string there, short strings wound round the spacelike circles of the contracting region and long strings wound round the timelike circles beyond it, and found tunnelling between them to be pair production of winding strings, as in the Schwinger effect [berkooz2004].

related.text: Misner space is Minkowski space with each event identified with its images under a boost [misner1967].
Misner space is Taub-NUT with the curvature taken out: the same horizon and the same closed timelike curves in flat space [misner1967].
James Grant showed in 1993 that Gott's two strings, away from the strings themselves, make a generalised Misner space, identified under a boost combined with a shift [grant1993].
The same construction in anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions, where the identification makes a black hole [banados1993].

A wormhole whose mouths move toward each other has a Cauchy horizon like Misner's with closed timelike curves behind it, and Kim and Thorne found the vacuum stress energy diverging there too [morris1988prl, kim1991].
Misner space with a gravitational wave added. Amos Ori's vacuum core of 2005 is curved, and its closed null geodesics are isolated circles, where Misner's fill the whole horizon [ori2005].
A bubble whose inside is Misner space's Rindler region, the time $\eta$ running once round $2\pi$, set in Minkowski space by a wall of exotic matter [tippett2017].

De Sitter space with events identified under the antipodal map of its hyperboloid, where Misner space identifies them under a boost. The antipodal map makes no closed timelike curves, and it removes the global direction of time [parikh2003].

Friedmann universes with points of space identified under translations, as events are identified here under a boost. The translations make space a torus and no closed timelike curve [lachiezerey1995].

De Sitter space identified under a boost, which a conformal map relates to Misner space. Gott and Li carried the Rindler vacuum across in 1998 and found its stress energy finite on the horizon when the boost has rapidity $2\pi$ [gott1998].
Anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions cut and glued under several boosts at once. Each black hole's singularity is of the kind Misner space has, with the curvature finite [brill1996].

coordinates.name: Misner

parameters.description: Period of $\psi$; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\psi_0/2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, \psi, y, z)$, with $T$ carrying dimensions of area, $\psi$ dimensionless and periodic with period $\psi_0$, and $y$ and $z$ lengths. No coordinate carries dimensions of time, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Milne

parameters.description: Twice the period of $\chi$; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\psi_0/2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \chi, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $\chi$ dimensionless and periodic with period $\psi_0/2$, and $y$ and $z$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Rindler

parameters.description: Twice the period of $\eta$; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\psi_0/2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\eta, \xi, y, z)$, with $\eta$ dimensionless and periodic with period $\psi_0/2$, and $\xi$, $y$, and $z$ lengths. No coordinate carries dimensions of time, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
